note: The Scriptorium's pens (docs/inklings-typography.md §3). A nib is not a cosmetic variant: each type produces the stress model a whole Vox-ATypI branch is CLASSIFIED by, so this table and data/typefaces.json's tree are the same information seen twice. Widths are em units, matching data/wordshape-alphabet.json's coordinate space; angles are degrees, ABSOLUTE (the pen angle a calligrapher holds, never tangent-relative — tangent-relative makes every stroke the same width and erases the lesson).

types.round: Constant width, w == h. No contrast at all, which is the whole of Lineal (sans) and, with terminals added later, Mechanistic.
types.broad: A rect of w x h held at a fixed absolute angle. Thick across the edge, thin along it — the ANGLED stress of the Humanist, Garalde and Calligraphic branches.
types.pointed: A flexible point that spreads under pressure, and pressure falls on the downstroke: width follows |dy|^pow. VERTICAL stress, hairline horizontals — Transitional, Didone, Script.

nibs.name: Round monoline
nibs.note: Owned from the start — the hand you already write in. One pen serves all three Lineal leaves, because a monoline HAS no contrast: the sans branch is not a pen distinction, which is itself the lesson.

nibs.name: Round, slab
nibs.note: Monoline like the sans pens; what makes a slab a slab is the TERMINAL, which is §3's later knob and not a nib property.

nibs.name: Broad, flat 10°
nibs.note: The flat pen of the insular scribes — nearly horizontal, so horizontals go thick and the forms go round.

nibs.name: Broad 30°
nibs.note: The steeper humanist pen — the one that slants the e-bar.

nibs.name: Pointed
nibs.note: The pen mid-turn: stress turning vertical, but the contrast still moderate.

nibs.name: Pointed, flexed
nibs.note: Maximum flex — fat stems, hairline horizontals. The engraver's answer to the quill.

nibs.name: Round, bold
nibs.note: No face of its own. Here because §10's claim — BOLD IS A WIDER NIB — should be visible in the bench before the style axis is ever built.
